Fifteen comments

Trip to Miriams

This was written by Colin Farrell and is played in many sessions around Manchester.

↳ Posted by jimbob on January 21st, 2005.

It sounds fantastic in A as well, especially on fiddle - you can get the rolls on the E then, rather than triplets or hammers on the open A.

↳ Posted by tbag on January 22nd, 2005.

this is also the first tune of brian finnegans performance track on his mad for trad whistle tutor

↳ Posted by ruairc on June 21st, 2006.

actually sorry - the second tune is trip to miriams. The first is dan breens or kevin burkes (recorded by dervish and many others)

↳ Posted by ruairc on June 21st, 2006.

Trip to Miriam’s

This was requested by a user on Chiff & Fipple. Liz Doherty seems to be the main recorded source, but this transcription is from the “Dave Williams Tribute Session 06” movie clip on Kerrywhistles.com (in the Cinema section). The tune starts at 24:13 in the video.

Since the box, whistle and banjo play slightly different settings, I’ve transcribed a slightly “normalized” version.

The sycopated section in the B part has several different variations, including |EAA FAA GAA|FAA EFAB| and |EAA DAA CA|A DAA EFAB| and |CAA DAA EA|A DAA EFAB|.

↳ Posted by MTGuru on December 4th, 2006.

Didn’t Colin Farrell pen this one?

↳ Posted by Will Harmon on December 4th, 2006.

Yes, sorry. Composed by fiddler / whistler Colin Farrell. Credit where due!

I met Colin and Co. when Gráda came through town this year. A great band, really nice people, and mighty musicians.
